name: Slite
description: Workspace docs, channels, users, groups, comments, verification, collections, and structured document editing through Slite's hosted MCP.
agentUseSummary: Connect once through Slite OAuth, then let agents use every documented read or write MCP tool under Safe or Dangerously skip permissions.

capabilities.label: Read workspace knowledge
capabilities.description: Ask, search, retrieve docs, inspect channels, users, groups, comments, recent activity, and knowledge-management queues.

capabilities.label: Create and maintain knowledge
capabilities.description: Create, update, move, archive, restore, verify, comment on, and structurally edit permitted Slite content.

allowed.label: Use read tools
allowed.description: Use one exact documented Slite MCP read tool with bounded arguments and live schema validation.

approvalRequired.label: Use write tools
approvalRequired.description: Use one exact documented Slite MCP mutation tool; Safe mode requires approval.

approvalProfiles.label: Safe
approvalProfiles.description: Documented reads run directly; every create, update, move, archive, restore, verification, comment, and structural mutation requires approval.

approvalProfiles.label: Dangerously skip permissions
approvalProfiles.description: Every selected OAuth-authorized Slite MCP operation runs without Relay per-action approval; ownership, OAuth scope, exact tool allowlists, bounds, audits, schema validation, and Slite permissions still apply.

runtimeSupport.description: Railway mounts exact read/write wrappers and proxies Slite OAuth to its hosted MCP.

providerSetup.blocker: Relay's public PKCE client is dynamically registered and its client ID is configured on Railway, but no signed-in Slite user session was available for production OAuth and action acceptance.
providerSetup.nextAction: A Slite user clicks Connect, approves read/write MCP access, then Relay runs OAuth callback, refresh, MCP health, a bounded search, and an approved or Dangerous-mode mutation.

evidence.supports: Slite documents its only supported remote MCP at https://api.slite.com/mcp, OAuth sign-in, and the complete current read/write tool list.
Slite publishes MCP resource metadata with its authorization server and openid, email, mcp:read, mcp:write, and offline_access scopes.
Slite publishes authorization, token, JWKS, and dynamic registration endpoints with authorization-code, refresh-token, S256 PKCE, and public-client support.
Slite states that the hosted MCP uses OAuth, preserves existing permissions, and supports search, retrieval, creation, updates, recent docs, directory discovery, and block editing.
Slite's separate REST v1 API uses customer-owned personal API keys; Relay prefers the official one-click hosted MCP OAuth path and does not misrepresent personal keys as OAuth.
